hypothesis: A lead-directed scalar decoder may reduce the per-byte table lookups and state-dependent transitions of the supplied DFA on mixed-width input by validating continuation bytes directly per code point, while retaining the ASCII-run fast path. This may instead lose from its lead-classification branches; controller measurement is needed.
notes: This is a pure-scalar variant. The supplied baseline is correct on 18 cases and measured 49.623 microseconds mean across three samples (baseline-e1); this candidate has not been measured. The prior h01 attempt was incorrect: its correctness log reports a failure at n=1024, seed 23, pattern 0 (errors=1, max_abs_error=1.0); the available diagnostic is truncated, so its cause is unknown.
transformations: Replace the byte-class and DFA transition tables with direct lead-range classification and continuation-byte checks grouped by UTF-8 sequence length.
Retain the ASCII-run scan and validate E0/ED and F0/F4 boundary restrictions explicitly.
Check remaining input length before each continuation-byte read to preserve bounds and malformed-input rejection.
